anomalies.description: Two police officers in riot gear physically restrain and appear to arrest a person wearing a blue head covering near a doorway; visible grappling and forceful contact.
A person is on the ground amid heavy smoke while multiple officers stand over them; one officer appears to strike or press down on the individual, suggesting abuse of a helpless person.

An armored police vehicle advances through a smoke-filled street while protesters confront it, some throwing objects (e.g., orange container at f4), others filming or raising hands; ongoing violent unrest with active engagement between groups.

A violent street confrontation involving Seattle Police in riot gear and protesters, with deployment of chemical agents (tear gas or smoke) and physical clashes; visible through multiple frames showing officers advancing, protesters on the ground, and dense smoke.
A sudden, bright white flash and rapidly expanding cloud consistent with a pyrotechnic canister detonation (e.g., tear gas or stun grenade) in the street, observed between frames f5 and f6.

A sudden, intense white flash and rapidly expanding cloud originate from a low point near a trash bin or container in the intersection, indicating a rapid energy release (e.g., incendiary device or flashbang). The cloud expands significantly within 1 second, characteristic of an explosion rather than sustained fire or slow smoke release.

A large plume of white smoke or gas erupts in the middle of a street intersection, with multiple individuals present including a crouching person filming and others moving away or observing; background shows urban setting with buildings and scattered debris, consistent with a protest or civil unrest involving pyrotechnics or tear gas.

A single explosion icon appears at Pacific Place (intersection of 6th Ave and Olive Way) and remains visible through frame f3 (293.5s).; A second explosion icon appears near Seafirst (intersection of 5th Ave and Olive Way), visible in frames f4–f6, while the first explosion at Pacific Place persists.; A third explosion icon appears at West Lake Center (intersection of 5th Ave and Pine St), visible from f7 onward; all three explosion icons remain present through f15.

A group of individuals, many wearing masks and dark clothing, collectively overturn and dismantle newspaper dispensers (including yellow 'DISPATCH' and red units) and knock over cardboard boxes labeled 'SEATTLE WEEKLY'. The coordinated destruction of public property, including lifting and carrying away a large blue dispenser, indicates violent unrest rather than peaceful protest.
A person in black hooded clothing is seen aiming and discharging a firearm at a building window; glass shatters visibly in subsequent frames (f8–f10), consistent with gunfire impact.
Two individuals in dark clothing appear to engage in physical struggle near the window during the apparent shooting event; one is pushed or falls backward in f9, suggesting mutual physical contact.

A broader scene of collective violent unrest unfolds, with multiple groups engaged in physical clashes, bystanders observing or intervening, and property damage (window smashing) occurring later in the sequence. The sustained intensity and scale beyond a single fight support classification as a riot.

A multi-person physical altercation occurs on the sidewalk, involving at least four individuals: a person in a red beret and red skirt, a person in a grey hoodie, a person in camouflage gear, and a person in a black jacket. They are seen grappling, pushing, and striking each other across frames f0–f6.

In frames f4–f5, a person in a grey hoodie appears to deliver a forceful kick to a person in camouflage who is off-balance and partially restrained, suggesting an attack on a vulnerable individual during the melee.

A separate violent incident occurs where a person in black hooded clothing repeatedly strikes a large glass storefront window with their fists, causing visible damage; this constitutes property-directed fighting/vandalism within the larger unrest.
